title: ContextAdapt: Evaluating Contextual Adaptation and Value Alignment in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2609.38260v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Values such as honesty, autonomy, and confidentiality are often regarded as general principles underpinning AI alignment. However, what it means to act in accordance with these values can depend on the context in which a decision is made. In this paper, we ask whether large language models (LLMs) appropriately adapt the application of a value across professional settings, while remaining consistent when contextual changes do not alter the relevant professional norm. To study this, we introduce ContextAdapt, an evaluation framework covering honesty, autonomy, and confidentiality across medicine, law, finance, and national security. Drawing on primary-source professional and regulatory documents, we construct a value x domain framework and use this to develop scenarios testing both default professional rules and recognised exceptions. translated_abstract: 诸如诚实、自主和保密等价值观常被视为支撑AI对齐的一般原则。然而，如何依照这些价值观行事，可能取决于做出决策时所处的具体情境。本文探究大语言模型（LLM）能否在跨越不同专业场景时恰当地调整价值观的应用方式，同时当情境变化并未改变相关职业规范时保持行为的一致性。为此，我们提出了ContextAdapt，一个覆盖医学、法律、金融和国家安全四大领域中诚实、自主与保密价值观的评估框架。基于一手专业与监管文件，我们构建了“价值观×领域”框架，并据此设计了测试默认职业规则及公认例外情形的多种场景。我们从模型推荐的行为及其给出的理由两个维度对12个大语言模型进行了评估。在我们的主要（评估中）
tldr: 提出了ContextAdapt评估框架，通过基于职业与监管一手文件构建的“价值观×领域”场景，考察12个大语言模型能否在医学、法律、金融和国家安全等领域恰当调整诚实、自主、保密等价值观的应用，并在规范未变时保持一致。
en_tdlr: Introduces ContextAdapt, a "value × domain" evaluation framework built from primary professional and regulatory sources that tests whether 12 LLMs appropriately adapt values like honesty, autonomy, and confidentiality across medicine, law, finance, and national security, while remaining consistent when professional norms are unchanged.
